ABS Non-Conformity : Requirement:
As per ISM Code, Clause 1, paragraph 1.2.3.1:
“The safety management system should ensure:
.1 compliance with mandatory rules and regulations.”
In this respect, reference is made to the following STCW Code requirements:
As per STCW Code, Section A-VIII/1, paragraph 1:
“Administrations shall, for the purpose of preventing fatigue:
establish and enforce rest periods for watchkeeping personnel; and
require that watch systems are so arranged that the efficiency of all watchkeeping personnel is not impaired by fatigue and that duties are so organized that the first watch at the commencement of a voyage and subsequent relieving watches are sufficiently rested and otherwise fit for duty.”
As per STCW Code, Section A-VIII/1, paragraph 3:
“The hours of rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which shall be at least 6 hours in length, and the intervals between consecutive periods of rest shall not exceed 14 hours.”
Evidence:
Upon sampling of crew work and rest hour records, inconsistencies were identified, as follows:
The work and rest hours record of AB King Philip Ceazar indicated a rest period from 08:00 to 16:00 on 14 August 2026. However, according to the Training or Drill Record, Form FM-0804-1, the seafarer participated in a fire drill conducted between 13:30 and 14:00 on the same date. The work and rest hours record therefore did not reflect the actual activity performed, and the required eight-hour continuous rest period was compromised.
The work and rest hours record of Chief Mate Valentino Charles for August 2026 showed multiple days on which the rest periods were divided into more than two periods within a 24-hour period. Short work periods ranging from approximately 30 minutes up to 3 hours resulted in up to five rest periods being recorded within a 24-hour period.
Nature of Non-Conformity:
Work and rest hour records were found inaccurate and did not demonstrate compliance with the required rest-period arrangement.
